Eli: quick note — did a fast sweep comparing per-channel vs per-tensor calibration on our fp8/int8 mixed kernels for 7B. results are... kinda noisy :thinking:
Sana: oof, noisy how? numbers plz
Eli: pasted the commands I ran and the summary below. sampling used a 10k-prod-trace subset (random 0.5%) + 2k curated prompts for stress. KV warmup included (1 prefix step).
```bash
# sampling (local harness)
python tools/quant_eval.py --model-rev v7b-r1 --dataset samples/10k_prod_05pct.jsonl --calib-mode per-channel --precision fp8 --kv-warmup 1 --runs 3 --out results/pc_fp8.json
python tools/quant_eval.py --model-rev v7b-r1 --dataset samples/curated_2k.jsonl --calib-mode per-tensor --precision int8 --kv-warmup 1 --runs 3 --out results/pt_int8.json
```
Eli: summary (median over runs):
- per-channel fp8: latency +6% vs fp32, tokens/s 1420, avg PPL +1.6% on prod subset, tail 99.9th err spike observed on ~0.3% of samples
- per-tensor int8: latency +3% vs fp32, tokens/s 1560, avg PPL +2.4% on prod subset, tail more stable but worse avg PPL on curated stress set (+3.1%)
Sana: interesting — pc better on avg PPL but worse tail, pt worse avg but smoother tail. could be outliers in prod trace skewing pc calibration?
Priya: did you try excluding very long sequences / extreme tokens? those can blow per-channel scales during calibration. what cutoff did you use?
Eli: no hard length cutoff, I only excluded samples with tokens > 4096 since our max context. tail samples were length ~1200-1800 mostly.
Jasper: FYI per-channel calibration is more sensitive to a few extreme rows in weight distribution. I've seen single-example activation peaks change scale by 30% and wreck quant for that channel.
Priya: that suggests we need an outlier policy. options: clip activations by percentile (99.5/99.9), use robust stats (MAD), or do weighted sampling so long tails get underweighted in the calib hist.
Sana: i prefer percentile clipping + stratified sampling (by length and prompt type). keep a small held-out set of 'adversarial' prompts to avoid regressing on tails.
Jasper: I worry percentile clipping will hide real long-tail workload behavior for customers who do long prompts. maybe we should do dual calibrations: primary per-channel with clipped stats, fallback per-tensor for long inputs? runtime can route based on length.
Eli: routing by length is doable (we already route larger seqs to dedicated kernels), but that increases complexity for model rollout. Also increased binary/kernel surface area.
Priya: alternative: compute per-channel scale but cap scale changes relative to per-tensor baseline (like max 2x deviation). that keeps per-channel benefits but bounds catastrophic channels.
Sana: that sounds promising. maybe algorithm: compute per-tensor scale S_t and per-channel S_c; final scale = clamp(S_c, S_t/clip_factor, S_t*clip_factor). clip_factor tuned on eval set (start with 2.0).
Eli: ran a quick patch for clamp factor 2.0 on the pc fp8 run — tail 99.9th err dropped 60%, avg PPL stayed within +0.2% of unclamped pc.
Jasper: nice. what about calibration dataset selection? i worry our 'prod trace subset' has ephemeral spikes from test harnesses and bots. we should filter by user-agent and remove internal-service calls.
Priya: agree. also weight samples by token frequency: rare tokens get boosted so we don't under-quantize them entirely. but that can hurt latency if rare tokens are noisy.
Sana: proposed dataset composition for next experiment: 70% filtered prod (no internal bots, dedup top identical prefixes), 20% curated stress (long prompts, multilingual, code), 10% adversarial tail set. use stratified sampling by length buckets [<64, 64-256, 256-1024, >1024].
Eli: we'll append a small metadata field per sample indicating URL/ref so it's auditable. also log which samples are driving per-channel extremes.
Jasper: metric-wise let's track: median tokens/s, 95/99/99.9 quant error percentiles, PPL delta, and end-to-end latency under KV warmup/no-warmup.
infra-bot: deploy-test started for job quant/tune/2164012345 (3 runs). logs -> https://ci.redwood/quant/2164012345
Priya: action items
- Priya: prepare cleaned prod subset + stratified sampler (ETA EOD)
- Eli: add clamp-to-pt baseline in quant_eval and rerun for fp8/int8/4bit mixes (ETA tomorrow)
- Jasper: add instrumentation to record which channels exceeded clip thresholds and export top-10 offenders per run
- Sana: run A/B harness (canary rollout) with KV-warmup/no-warmup buckets once results ready
Sana: small ask — include seed + exact harness command in artifacts so runs are reproducible.
Eli: yup will push raw logs + harness commands.
Priya: one more thought — for model rollout, recommend automatic fallback policy: if 99.9th quant error > threshold on canary, revert to per-tensor until fix. avoids blips in production.
Jasper: agreed. also add a daily regression check vs baseline using the curated stress set.
Sana: sounds like a plan. thanks everyone :thumbsup:
Eli: thanks — i'll post the first run summary here when CI finishes.
